title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). A is an F_p-algebra, B an A-algebra, F_A: A→A the Frobenius x↦x^p, Ã = A viewed as an A-algebra through F_A, and B̃ = B⊗_{A,F_A} A the Frobenius twist. The relative Frobenius B̃→B, b⊗a ↦ a·b^p, has image Λ = A[B^p]. Earlier pages built a ring homomorphism ψ: Ω*_{B/A} → Z*(B/A) with ψ(x) = x^p and ψ(dx) = x^{p-1}dx. It is semilinear over B→B̃ and so linearizes to a Λ-algebra map Ω*_{B̃/Ã} → Z*. Composing with Z*→H*_DR gives φ: Ω*_{B̃/Ã} → H*_DR(B/A), the inverse Cartier map.

Theorem 1 (this page). Suppose B/A has a p-basis (x_i)_{i∈I}, i.e. B is free over Λ on the monomials x^α with 0≤α_i<p. Then:
- φ induces an isomorphism Ω*_{B̃/Ã}⊗_{B̃}Λ ≅ H*_DR(B/A).
- Hence φ itself is an isomorphism when B̃→B is injective, i.e. B̃ ≅ Λ.

Proof sketch.
- With B_i = Λ[x_i], B ≅ ⊗_{Λ,i} B_i and Ω*_{B/A} ≅ ⊗_i Ω*_{B_i/Λ}, a tensor product of complexes of free Λ-modules.
- Künneth over Λ gives H*_DR(B/A) ≅ ⊗_i H*_DR(B_i/Λ), and the Frobenius-twisted side decomposes the same way.
- φ is the tensor product of the one-variable maps φ_i. Each sends the basis (1, dx̃_i) to the basis (1, x_i^{p-1}dx_i) of H*(B_i/Λ), which a direct computation for Λ[x]/(x^p − a) confirms.

Corollary 1. Z* ≅ B* ⊕ (Ω*_{B̃/Ã}⊗Λ) as Λ-modules. This splitting holds because the cohomology is Λ-free; it is not canonical.

Definition. The inverse of φ is the Cartier operation C̃: H*_DR(B/A) ≅ Ω*_{B̃/Ã}⊗_{B̃}Λ = Ω*_{B/A}⊗_{B,F}Λ. Its lift C̃: Z*(B/A) → Ω*_{B̃/Ã}(⊗Λ) is surjective on closed forms and kills exact forms.

Role in the dossier. This is the standard Cartier isomorphism, written in relative form with a p-basis hypothesis. It is preparatory material for the treatment of Gauss–Manin connections and p-curvature in the same file (Katz's 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' circle).
errors: Minor: the target of C̃ on Z* is written Ω*_{B̃/Ã}. Unless B̃→Λ is an isomorphism it should be Ω*_{B̃/Ã}⊗_{B̃}Λ, which the parenthetical identification on the page acknowledges.
Corollary 1's direct-sum decomposition is only a non-canonical splitting of Λ-modules. It relies on H*_DR being Λ-free, which the p-basis gives.
In the proof, the tensor products ⊗_i should be over Λ, giving Ω*_{B/A} ≅ ⊗_Λ Ω*_{B_i/Λ}. The notation '⊗_{B_i} B' is loose.

ideas.what: Inverse Cartier map φ: Ω*_{B̃/Ã} → H*_DR(B/A), dx̃ ↦ [x^{p-1}dx], and the theorem that it is an isomorphism (after ⊗Λ) for algebras with a p-basis
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Cartier (1957); relative form in N. Katz (1970, Publ. IHES 39, §7); Deligne–Illusie (1987)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; the standard reference is Katz 1970, whose results were developed in dialogue with Grothendieck

ideas.what: Proof by reduction via a p-basis to one variable, using Künneth for de Rham complexes over Λ = A[B^p]
ideas.modern_name: p-basis computation of de Rham cohomology in char p

ideas.what: Characterisation of C̃ on closed forms: kills exact forms, multiplicative, sends x^{p-1}dx to dx̃, and sends dlog to dlog

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard exposition of the Cartier isomorphism for algebras with a p-basis. The only slight nuance is formulating it with ⊗Λ, without assuming the relative Frobenius is injective, and that nuance is also present in standard treatments. Nothing here is absent from the literature (Cartier, Katz 1970, Deligne–Illusie).
transcription_corrections: 'donc est un isom. si B̃ → A' should read 'si B̃ → Λ (iso), i.e. B̃ → B est injectif'.
'[NB Λ ≃ B̃/id?]' is most likely 'Λ ≃ B̃/idéal (noyau)', i.e. Λ is the quotient of B̃ by the kernel of relative Frobenius.
'Cm.' before Corollaire 1 is likely an abbreviation such as 'On a' or 'Comme'.
'Ω*_{B/A} ≃ ⊗ Ω*_{B_i/Λ} ⊗_{B_i} B' — the encircled marginal note reads 'isom. de B-alg.'.
